74	class OzaBagging(AbstractClassifier):
75	    """Online bagging of Hoeffding Trees with Poisson(1) resampling.
76	
77	    Each of the ``num_learners`` base learners trains on every arriving example
78	    ``k ~ Poisson(1)`` times, which simulates drawing a bootstrap replicate of
79	    the stream.  Predictions are combined by a majority vote over the base
80	    learners.
81	
82	    Args:
83	        num_learners: Size ``N`` of the ensemble.
84	        seed: Seed of the ``random.Random`` used for the Poisson draws.
85	        num_classes: Number of classes (passed on to the base learners).
86	        num_attributes: Number of attributes (passed on to the base learners).
87	        grace_period: ``n_min`` of the base Hoeffding Trees.
88	        split_confidence: ``delta`` of the base Hoeffding Trees.
89	        tie_threshold: ``tau`` of the base Hoeffding Trees.
90	        max_depth: Maximum depth of the base Hoeffding Trees.
91	        num_bins: Bins of the numeric attribute observers.
92	        lam: Rate of the Poisson resampling distribution (1.0 in Oza bagging).
93	        base_learner_factory: Optional ``callable(index) -> classifier`` used
94	            instead of the default Hoeffding Tree factory.
95	    """
96	
97	    def __init__(self,
98	                 num_learners: int = 10,
99	                 seed: int = 42,
100	                 num_classes: Optional[int] = None,
101	                 num_attributes: Optional[int] = None,
102	                 grace_period: int = 200,
103	                 split_confidence: float = 1e-7,
104	                 tie_threshold: float = 0.05,
105	                 max_depth: int = 20,
106	                 num_bins: int = 10,
107	                 lam: float = 1.0,
108	                 base_learner_factory: Optional[Callable[[int], object]] = None):
109	        super().__init__()
110	        self.num_learners = int(num_learners)
111	        self.seed = int(seed)
112	        self.num_classes = num_classes if num_classes else 0
113	        self.num_attributes = num_attributes if num_attributes else 0
114	        self.grace_period = int(grace_period)
115	        self.split_confidence = float(split_confidence)
116	        self.tie_threshold = float(tie_threshold)
117	        self.max_depth = int(max_depth)
118	        self.num_bins = int(num_bins)
119	        self.lam = float(lam)
120	        self.base_learner_factory = base_learner_factory
121	
122	        self.rng = random.Random(self.seed)
123	        #: number of examples each base learner was trained on
124	        self.learner_weights: List[float] = [0.0] * self.num_learners
125	        self.learners: List[object] = [self._new_learner(index)
126	                                       for index in range(self.num_learners)]
127	
128	    # -- construction ------------------------------------------------------
129	    def _new_learner(self, index: int):
130	        if self.base_learner_factory is not None:
131	            return self.base_learner_factory(index)
132	        return HoeffdingTree(num_attributes=self.num_attributes or None,
133	                             num_classes=self.num_classes or None,
134	                             grace_period=self.grace_period,
135	                             split_confidence=self.split_confidence,
136	                             tie_threshold=self.tie_threshold,
137	                             max_depth=self.max_depth,
138	                             num_bins=self.num_bins)
139	
140	    # -- training ----------------------------------------------------------
141	    def train(self, instance: Instance):
142	        """Train every base learner ``k ~ Poisson(lam)`` times on ``instance``."""
143	        if instance.label is not None and instance.label + 1 > self.num_classes:
144	            self.num_classes = instance.label + 1
145	        if instance.num_attributes > self.num_attributes:
146	            self.num_attributes = instance.num_attributes
147	        self.instances_seen += 1
148	        for index, learner in enumerate(self.learners):
149	            k = poisson(self.lam, self.rng)
150	            if k <= 0:
151	                continue
152	            self.learner_weights[index] += k
153	            for _ in range(k):
154	                learner.train(instance)
155	
156	    def partial_fit(self, instance: Instance):
157	        """Alias for :meth:`train`."""
158	        self.train(instance)
159	
160	    # -- prediction --------------------------------------------------------
161	    def get_votes(self, instance: Instance) -> Dict[int, float]:
162	        """Majority vote: one vote per base learner that has an opinion."""
163	        votes: Dict[int, float] = {}
164	        for learner in self.learners:
165	            learner_votes = learner.get_votes(instance)
166	            if not learner_votes:
167	                continue
168	            best_class = -1
169	            best_weight = float("-inf")
170	            for cls in sorted(learner_votes):
171	                weight = learner_votes[cls]
172	                if weight > best_weight:
173	                    best_weight = weight
174	                    best_class = cls
175	            if best_class < 0:
176	                continue
177	            votes[best_class] = votes.get(best_class, 0.0) + 1.0
178	        return votes
179	
180	    def get_soft_votes(self, instance: Instance) -> Dict[int, float]:
181	        """Sum of the normalised class distributions of the base learners."""
182	        votes: Dict[int, float] = {}
183	        for learner in self.learners:
184	            learner_votes = learner.get_votes(instance)
185	            total = sum(learner_votes.values())
186	            if total <= 0:
187	                continue
188	            for cls, weight in learner_votes.items():
189	                votes[cls] = votes.get(cls, 0.0) + weight / total
190	        return votes
191	
192	    def predict(self, instance: Instance) -> int:
193	        votes = self.get_votes(instance)
194	        if not votes:
195	            return 0
196	        best_class = -1
197	        best_weight = float("-inf")
198	        for cls in sorted(votes):
199	            weight = votes[cls]
200	            if weight > best_weight:
201	                best_weight = weight
202	                best_class = cls
203	        return best_class if best_class >= 0 else 0
204	
205	    def predict_proba(self, instance: Instance) -> Dict[int, float]:
206	        votes = self.get_votes(instance)
207	        total = sum(votes.values())
208	        if total <= 0:
209	            return {}
210	        return {cls: weight / total for cls, weight in votes.items()}
211	
212	    # -- introspection -----------------------------------------------------
213	    def get_ensemble_size(self) -> int:
214	        return len(self.learners)
215	
216	    def get_tree_sizes(self) -> List[Dict[str, int]]:
217	        sizes = []
218	        for learner in self.learners:
219	            getter = getattr(learner, "get_tree_size", None)
220	            sizes.append(getter() if getter is not None else {})
221	        return sizes
222	
223	    def get_total_nodes(self) -> int:
224	        return sum(size.get("total_nodes", 0) for size in self.get_tree_sizes())
225	
226	    def get_average_tree_nodes(self) -> float:
227	        sizes = self.get_tree_sizes()
228	        if not sizes:
229	            return 0.0
230	        return self.get_total_nodes() / len(sizes)
231	
232	    def reset(self):
233	        self.instances_seen = 0
234	        self.rng = random.Random(self.seed)
235	        self.learner_weights = [0.0] * self.num_learners
236	        self.learners = [self._new_learner(index)
237	                         for index in range(self.num_learners)]
238	
239	    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
240	        return ("OzaBagging(num_learners=%d, nodes=%d)"
241	                % (len(self.learners), self.get_total_nodes()))

249	class EvaluateInterleavedTestThenTrain:
250	    """The MOA ``EvaluateInterleavedTestThenTrain`` task.
251	
252	    Every example of the stream is first classified (test) and then handed to
253	    the learner (train), so no example is ever used for testing after it has
254	    been learnt.  Accuracy is reported cumulatively and over a sliding window,
255	    with a snapshot recorded every ``sample_frequency`` examples.
256	
257	    Args:
258	        classifier: Learner implementing ``predict`` and ``train``.
259	        stream: Stream generator to draw the examples from.
260	        num_instances: Number of examples to process.
261	        window_size: Length of the sliding accuracy window.
262	        sample_frequency: Number of examples between two accuracy snapshots.
263	        name: Optional label used in the returned metadata.
264	    """
265	
266	    def __init__(self, classifier, stream: StreamGenerator,
267	                 num_instances: int = 100000, window_size: int = 1000,
268	                 sample_frequency: int = 10000, name: Optional[str] = None):
269	        self.classifier = classifier
270	        self.stream = stream
271	        self.num_instances = int(num_instances)
272	        self.window_size = int(window_size)
273	        self.sample_frequency = max(1, int(sample_frequency))
274	        self.name = name or type(classifier).__name__
275	        self.evaluator = PrequentialEvaluator(window_size=self.window_size)
276	        #: accuracy snapshots taken every ``sample_frequency`` examples
277	        self.snapshots: List[Dict[str, float]] = []
278	        self.result: Dict[str, object] = {}
279	
280	    # -- task --------------------------------------------------------------
281	    def run(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
282	        """Run the task and return the collected measurements."""
283	        evaluator = self.evaluator
284	        evaluator.reset()
285	        self.snapshots = []
286	        classifier = self.classifier
287	        stream = self.stream
288	        start = time.time()
289	        for index in range(1, self.num_instances + 1):
290	            instance = stream.next_instance()
291	            prediction = classifier.predict(instance)
292	            evaluator.add_result(prediction, instance.label)
293	            classifier.train(instance)
294	            if index % self.sample_frequency == 0:
295	                self.snapshots.append({
296	                    "instances": float(index),
297	                    "cumulative_accuracy": evaluator.get_cumulative_accuracy(),
298	                    "window_accuracy": evaluator.get_window_accuracy(),
299	                })
300	        elapsed = time.time() - start
301	
302	        self.result = {
303	            "cumulative_accuracy": evaluator.get_cumulative_accuracy(),
304	            "window_accuracy": evaluator.get_window_accuracy(),
305	            "snapshots": self.snapshots,
306	            "learning_curve": [(int(s["instances"]), s["window_accuracy"])
307	                               for s in self.snapshots],
308	            "metadata": self.get_metadata(elapsed),
309	        }
310	        return self.result
311	
312	    def get_metadata(self, elapsed: float = 0.0) -> Dict[str, object]:
313	        """Describe the run: learner, stream, sizes and timing."""
314	        metadata: Dict[str, object] = {
315	            "task": type(self).__name__,
316	            "name": self.name,
317	            "classifier": type(self.classifier).__name__,
318	            "stream": type(self.stream).__name__,
319	            "num_instances": self.num_instances,
320	            "instances_processed": self.evaluator.total_seen,
321	            "correct": self.evaluator.total_correct,
322	            "window_size": self.window_size,
323	            "sample_frequency": self.sample_frequency,
324	            "evaluation_time_seconds": elapsed,
325	        }
326	        if isinstance(self.classifier, OzaBagging):
327	            metadata["ensemble_size"] = self.classifier.get_ensemble_size()
328	            metadata["total_nodes"] = self.classifier.get_total_nodes()
329	        else:
330	            getter = getattr(self.classifier, "get_tree_size", None)
331	            if getter is not None:
332	                metadata["total_nodes"] = getter().get("total_nodes", 0)
333	        return metadata
334	
335	    # -- convenience -------------------------------------------------------
336	    def get_cumulative_accuracy(self) -> float:
337	        return self.evaluator.get_cumulative_accuracy()
338	
339	    def get_window_accuracy(self) -> float:
340	        return self.evaluator.get_window_accuracy()

349	    """Collect the metrics of several experiments and report them uniformly.

378	                   metrics: Sequence[str] = ("cumulative_accuracy",

1	"""ADWIN: ADaptive WINdowing for concept drift detection.
2	
3	Implementation of the change detector of Bifet & Gavalda, "Learning from
4	Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing", SDM 2007.
5	
6	ADWIN keeps a variable length window of the most recent observations, stored in
7	compressed form as an *exponential histogram*: a list of
8	:class:`BucketRow` objects where row ``i`` holds buckets summarising ``2^i``
9	observations each.  At most ``max_buckets_per_row`` buckets live in a row; when
10	a row overflows its two oldest buckets are merged into a single bucket of the
11	next row, so a window of ``n`` items needs only ``O(M log n)`` memory.
12	
13	After every insertion the window is scanned for a split point ``W = W0 . W1``
14	such that the means of the two sub-windows differ by more than the statistical
15	bound
16	
17	    epsilon = sqrt(2 * m * v * ln(2 ln n / delta')) + (2/3) * m * ln(2 ln n / delta')
18	
19	(the variance-sensitive bound of ADWIN2, with ``1/m = 1/n0 + 1/n1`` the
20	harmonic mean of the sub-window lengths and ``v`` the observed variance) or,
21	when ``use_variance_bound`` is disabled, the plain Hoeffding cut
22	
23	    epsilon = sqrt((1 / (2 m)) * ln(4 / delta'))     with delta' = delta / n.
24	
25	Whenever such a split exists the distribution has changed: the oldest bucket is
26	dropped and the test is repeated, so the window shrinks to the portion of the
27	stream that is consistent with the new concept.
28	"""

42	class Bucket:
43	    """Summary statistics of one segment of the window.
44	
45	    Attributes:
46	        total: Sum of the observations contained in the bucket.
47	        variance: Sum of squared deviations from the bucket mean.
48	        count: Number of observations summarised by the bucket.
49	    """
50	
51	    __slots__ = ("total", "variance", "count", "previous", "next")
52	
53	    def __init__(self, total: float = 0.0, variance: float = 0.0,
54	                 count: int = 0):
55	        self.total = float(total)
56	        self.variance = float(variance)
57	        self.count = int(count)
58	        self.previous: Optional["Bucket"] = None
59	        self.next: Optional["Bucket"] = None
60	
61	    # -- statistics --------------------------------------------------------
62	    @property
63	    def mean(self) -> float:
64	        if self.count <= 0:
65	            return 0.0
66	        return self.total / self.count
67	
68	    def clear(self):
69	        self.total = 0.0
70	        self.variance = 0.0
71	        self.count = 0
72	        self.previous = None
73	        self.next = None
74	
75	    def copy(self) -> "Bucket":
76	        return Bucket(self.total, self.variance, self.count)
77	
78	    # -- merging -----------------------------------------------------------
79	    def merge(self, other: "Bucket") -> "Bucket":
80	        """Merge the adjacent bucket ``other`` into this one.
81	
82	        The variance of the union of two samples follows from
83	
84	            V = V_a + V_b + n_a n_b (mean_a - mean_b)^2 / (n_a + n_b)
85	
86	        Returns ``self`` so that merges can be chained.
87	        """
88	        if other is None or other.count == 0:
89	            return self
90	        if self.count == 0:
91	            self.total = other.total
92	            self.variance = other.variance
93	            self.count = other.count
94	            return self
95	        n_a = self.count
96	        n_b = other.count
97	        mean_diff = self.total / n_a - other.total / n_b
98	        self.variance = (self.variance + other.variance
99	                         + n_a * n_b * mean_diff * mean_diff / (n_a + n_b))
100	        self.total += other.total
101	        self.count = n_a + n_b
102	        return self
103	
104	    @staticmethod
105	    def merged(first: "Bucket", second: "Bucket") -> "Bucket":
106	        """Return a new bucket holding the union of ``first`` and ``second``."""
107	        return first.copy().merge(second)
108	
109	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
110	        return ("Bucket(total=%.4f, variance=%.4f, count=%d)"
111	                % (self.total, self.variance, self.count))

114	class BucketRow:
115	    """Doubly linked list of :class:`Bucket` objects of the same granularity.
116	
117	    ``head`` is the *oldest* bucket of the row and ``tail`` the most recent one.
118	    Row ``level`` stores buckets summarising ``2 ** level`` observations.
119	    """
120	
121	    def __init__(self, level: int = 0):
122	        self.level = int(level)
123	        self.head: Optional[Bucket] = None
124	        self.tail: Optional[Bucket] = None
125	        self._size = 0
126	
127	    # -- properties --------------------------------------------------------
128	    @property
129	    def size(self) -> int:
130	        """Number of buckets currently stored in the row."""
131	        return self._size
132	
133	    @property
134	    def bucket_size(self) -> int:
135	        """Number of observations each bucket of this row summarises."""
136	        return 2 ** self.level
137	
138	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
139	        return self._size == 0
140	
141	    # -- list operations ---------------------------------------------------
142	    def add_to_tail(self, bucket: Bucket) -> Bucket:
143	        """Append ``bucket`` as the most recent bucket of the row."""
144	        bucket.previous = self.tail
145	        bucket.next = None
146	        if self.tail is not None:
147	            self.tail.next = bucket
148	        else:
149	            self.head = bucket
150	        self.tail = bucket
151	        self._size += 1
152	        return bucket
153	
154	    def add_to_head(self, bucket: Bucket) -> Bucket:
155	        """Insert ``bucket`` as the oldest bucket of the row."""
156	        bucket.previous = None
157	        bucket.next = self.head
158	        if self.head is not None:
159	            self.head.previous = bucket
160	        else:
161	            self.tail = bucket
162	        self.head = bucket
163	        self._size += 1
164	        return bucket
165	
166	    def remove_from_head(self) -> Optional[Bucket]:
167	        """Remove and return the oldest bucket of the row."""
168	        bucket = self.head
169	        if bucket is None:
170	            return None
171	        self.head = bucket.next
172	        if self.head is not None:
173	            self.head.previous = None
174	        else:
175	            self.tail = None
176	        self._size -= 1
177	        bucket.previous = None
178	        bucket.next = None
179	        return bucket
180	
181	    def remove_from_tail(self) -> Optional[Bucket]:
182	        """Remove and return the most recent bucket of the row."""
183	        bucket = self.tail
184	        if bucket is None:
185	            return None
186	        self.tail = bucket.previous
187	        if self.tail is not None:
188	            self.tail.next = None
189	        else:
190	            self.head = None
191	        self._size -= 1
192	        bucket.previous = None
193	        bucket.next = None
194	        return bucket
195	
196	    def clear(self):
197	        self.head = None
198	        self.tail = None
199	        self._size = 0
200	
201	    # -- iteration ---------------------------------------------------------
202	    def buckets(self) -> Iterator[Bucket]:
203	        """Iterate over the buckets from the oldest to the most recent one."""
204	        bucket = self.head
205	        while bucket is not None:
206	            yield bucket
207	            bucket = bucket.next
208	
209	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Bucket]:
210	        return self.buckets()
211	
212	    def __len__(self) -> int:
213	        return self._size
214	
215	    def total(self) -> float:
216	        return sum(bucket.total for bucket in self.buckets())
217	
218	    def count(self) -> int:
219	        return sum(bucket.count for bucket in self.buckets())
220	
221	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
222	        return "BucketRow(level=%d, size=%d)" % (self.level, self._size)

225	class ADWIN:
226	    """ADaptive WINdowing drift detector.
227	
228	    Args:
229	        delta: Confidence parameter of the change test.
230	        max_buckets_per_row: ``M``, buckets kept per granularity level.
231	        min_window_length: Minimum length of each sub-window when testing.
232	        min_clock: Run the change test every ``min_clock`` insertions.
233	        use_variance_bound: Use the variance sensitive ADWIN2 cut (default) or
234	            the plain Hoeffding cut of the original paper.
235	    """
236	
237	    def __init__(self, delta: float = 0.002, max_buckets_per_row: int = 5,
238	                 min_window_length: int = 10, min_clock: int = 1,
239	                 use_variance_bound: bool = True):
240	        self.delta = float(delta)
241	        self.max_buckets_per_row = int(max_buckets_per_row)
242	        self.min_window_length = int(min_window_length)
243	        self.min_clock = max(1, int(min_clock))
244	        self.use_variance_bound = bool(use_variance_bound)
245	        self.reset()
246	
247	    # -- state -------------------------------------------------------------
248	    def reset(self):
249	        """Clear all state (window, buckets and detection flags)."""
250	        self.bucket_rows: List[BucketRow] = [BucketRow(0)]
251	        self._width = 0
252	        self._total = 0.0
253	        self._variance_sum = 0.0
254	        self.bucket_count = 0
255	        self.time = 0
256	        self._detected_change = False
257	        self._detected_warning = False
258	        self.num_detections = 0
259	        self.num_elements = 0
260	        self.width_at_last_detection = 0
261	        self.detection_points: List[int] = []
262	
263	    # -- properties --------------------------------------------------------
264	    @property
265	    def width(self) -> int:
266	        """Current total window length."""
267	        return self._width
268	
269	    @property
270	    def total(self) -> float:
271	        """Running sum of the elements inside the window."""
272	        return self._total
273	
274	    @property
275	    def variance_sum(self) -> float:
276	        """Sum of squared deviations of the elements inside the window."""
277	        return self._variance_sum
278	
279	    @property
280	    def variance(self) -> float:
281	        """Running variance estimate of the elements inside the window."""
282	        if self._width <= 0:
283	            return 0.0
284	        return self._variance_sum / self._width
285	
286	    @property
287	    def last_bucket_row(self) -> int:
288	        return len(self.bucket_rows) - 1
289	
290	    def get_estimation(self) -> float:
291	        """Current mean estimate ``total / width``."""
292	        if self._width <= 0:
293	            return 0.0
294	        return self._total / self._width
295	
296	    # scikit-multiflow style aliases -------------------------------------
297	    @property
298	    def estimation(self) -> float:
299	        return self.get_estimation()
300	
301	    def get_width(self) -> int:
302	        return self._width
303	
304	    def get_total(self) -> float:
305	        return self._total
306	
307	    def get_variance(self) -> float:
308	        return self.variance
309	
310	    def get_num_buckets(self) -> int:
311	        return self.bucket_count
312	
313	    def detected_change(self) -> bool:
314	        """True when the most recent :meth:`add_element` detected a change."""
315	        return self._detected_change
316	
317	    def detected_warning_zone(self) -> bool:
318	        return self._detected_warning
319	
320	    # -- insertion ---------------------------------------------------------
321	    def add_element(self, value: float) -> bool:
322	        """Add an observation to the window and test for a distribution change.
323	
324	        Returns True when a change was detected (and the window shrunk).
325	        """
326	        value = float(value)
327	        self.time += 1
328	        self.num_elements += 1
329	        self._detected_change = False
330	
331	        self._insert_element(value)
332	        self._compress()
333	
334	        if self.time % self.min_clock == 0:
335	            changed = self._check_for_change()
336	        else:
337	            changed = False
338	        return changed
339	
340	    def add(self, value: float) -> bool:
341	        """Alias for :meth:`add_element`."""
342	        return self.add_element(value)
343	
344	    def update(self, value: float) -> bool:
345	        """Alias for :meth:`add_element` (scikit-multiflow naming)."""
346	        return self.add_element(value)
347	
348	    def _insert_element(self, value: float):
349	        """Insert ``value`` as a new bucket of size one at row 0."""
350	        self._width += 1
351	        self.bucket_rows[0].add_to_tail(Bucket(total=value, variance=0.0,
352	                                               count=1))
353	        self.bucket_count += 1
354	        if self._width > 1:
355	            previous_mean = self._total / (self._width - 1)
356	            deviation = value - previous_mean
357	            self._variance_sum += ((self._width - 1) * deviation * deviation
358	                                   / self._width)
359	        self._total += value
360	
361	    # -- compression -------------------------------------------------------
362	    def _compress(self):
363	        """Merge the two oldest buckets of every overflowing row."""
364	        row_index = 0
365	        while row_index < len(self.bucket_rows):
366	            row = self.bucket_rows[row_index]
367	            if row.size <= self.max_buckets_per_row:
368	                break
369	            first = row.remove_from_head()
370	            second = row.remove_from_head()
371	            if first is None or second is None:
372	                if first is not None:
373	                    row.add_to_head(first)
374	                break
375	            merged = first.merge(second)
376	            self.bucket_count -= 1
377	            if row_index + 1 >= len(self.bucket_rows):
378	                self.bucket_rows.append(BucketRow(row_index + 1))
379	            self.bucket_rows[row_index + 1].add_to_tail(merged)
380	            row_index += 1
381	
382	    # -- deletion ----------------------------------------------------------
383	    def _delete_element(self) -> int:
384	        """Drop the oldest bucket of the window; returns its element count."""
385	        row = self._oldest_row()
386	        if row is None:
387	            return 0
388	        bucket = row.remove_from_head()
389	        if bucket is None:
390	            return 0
391	        count = bucket.count
392	        self._width -= count
393	        self._total -= bucket.total
394	        self.bucket_count -= 1
395	        if self._width > 0 and count > 0:
396	            mean_removed = bucket.total / count
397	            mean_rest = self._total / self._width
398	            mean_diff = mean_removed - mean_rest
399	            self._variance_sum -= (bucket.variance
400	                                   + count * self._width * mean_diff * mean_diff
401	                                   / (count + self._width))
402	            if self._variance_sum < 0.0:
403	                self._variance_sum = 0.0
404	        elif self._width <= 0:
405	            self._variance_sum = 0.0
406	            self._total = 0.0
407	        # drop empty rows at the coarse end of the histogram
408	        while len(self.bucket_rows) > 1 and self.bucket_rows[-1].is_empty():
409	            self.bucket_rows.pop()
410	        return count
411	
412	    def _oldest_row(self) -> Optional[BucketRow]:
413	        for index in range(len(self.bucket_rows) - 1, -1, -1):
414	            if not self.bucket_rows[index].is_empty():
415	                return self.bucket_rows[index]
416	        return None
417	
418	    # -- change detection --------------------------------------------------
419	    def _iterate_buckets_oldest_first(self) -> Iterator[Bucket]:
420	        for index in range(len(self.bucket_rows) - 1, -1, -1):
421	            for bucket in self.bucket_rows[index].buckets():
422	                yield bucket
423	
424	    def cut_expression(self, n0: float, n1: float, u0: float, u1: float,
425	                       v0: float = 0.0, v1: float = 0.0) -> bool:
426	        """True when the means of the two sub-windows are significantly apart."""
427	        if n0 <= 0 or n1 <= 0:
428	            return False
429	        difference = u0 / n0 - u1 / n1
430	        return abs(difference) > self.epsilon_cut(n0, n1)
431	
432	    def epsilon_cut(self, n0: float, n1: float) -> float:
433	        """The statistical bound a mean difference has to exceed."""
434	        n = float(self._width)
435	        if n0 <= 0 or n1 <= 0 or n <= 1:
436	            return float("inf")
437	        if self.use_variance_bound:
438	            # ADWIN2: variance sensitive bound, delta' = delta / (2 ln n)
439	            log_n = math.log(n) if n > math.e else 1.0
440	            delta_prime = math.log(2.0 * log_n / self.delta)
441	            offset = self.min_window_length - 1
442	            inverse_m = (1.0 / max(1.0, n0 - offset)
443	                         + 1.0 / max(1.0, n1 - offset))
444	            variance = self.variance
445	            return (math.sqrt(2.0 * inverse_m * variance * delta_prime)
446	                    + 2.0 / 3.0 * delta_prime * inverse_m)
447	        # Original ADWIN cut: harmonic mean m and delta' = delta / n
448	        inverse_m = 1.0 / n0 + 1.0 / n1
449	        delta_prime = self.delta / n
450	        return math.sqrt(0.5 * inverse_m * math.log(4.0 / delta_prime))
451	
452	    def _check_for_change(self) -> bool:
453	        """Shrink the window while a significant split point exists."""
454	        changed = False
455	        keep_going = True
456	        while keep_going:
457	            keep_going = False
458	            if self._width < 2 * self.min_window_length:
459	                break
460	            n0 = 0.0
461	            u0 = 0.0
462	            v0 = 0.0
463	            n1 = float(self._width)
464	            u1 = self._total
465	            v1 = self._variance_sum
466	            for bucket in self._iterate_buckets_oldest_first():
467	                n2 = float(bucket.count)
468	                u2 = bucket.total
469	                if n2 <= 0:
470	                    continue
471	                rest = n1 - n2
472	                if rest <= 0:
473	                    break               # the newest bucket cannot be cut off
474	                # move the bucket from the newer sub-window to the older one
475	                if n0 > 0:
476	                    mean_diff = u0 / n0 - u2 / n2
477	                    v0 += (bucket.variance
478	                           + n0 * n2 * mean_diff * mean_diff / (n0 + n2))
479	                else:
480	                    v0 += bucket.variance
481	                mean_diff = u2 / n2 - (u1 - u2) / rest
482	                v1 -= bucket.variance + n2 * rest * mean_diff * mean_diff / n1
483	                if v1 < 0.0:
484	                    v1 = 0.0
485	                n0 += n2
486	                u0 += u2
487	                n1 = rest
488	                u1 -= u2
489	                if (n0 >= self.min_window_length
490	                        and n1 >= self.min_window_length
491	                        and self.cut_expression(n0, n1, u0, u1, v0, v1)):
492	                    changed = True
493	                    removed = self._delete_element()
494	                    if removed > 0:
495	                        keep_going = True
496	                    break
497	        if changed:
498	            self._detected_change = True
499	            self.num_detections += 1
500	            self.width_at_last_detection = self._width
501	            self.detection_points.append(self.num_elements)
502	        return changed
503

505	    def get_window_elements(self) -> List[Bucket]:
506	        """Buckets of the window from oldest to newest (debugging helper)."""
507	        return list(self._iterate_buckets_oldest_first())
508	
509	    def __len__(self) -> int:
510	        return self._width
511	
512	    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
513	        return ("ADWIN(width=%d, mean=%.4f, variance=%.4f, buckets=%d)"
514	                % (self._width, self.get_estimation(), self.variance,

27	class ADWINExperiment:
28	    """Drift detection experiments on synthetic streams.
29	
30	    Args:
31	        delta: ADWIN confidence parameter.
32	        num_samples: Length of the generated streams.
33	        change_point: Index of the abrupt change.
34	        sigma: Standard deviation of the Gaussian noise.
35	        max_buckets_per_row: ADWIN ``M`` parameter.
36	        min_window_length: ADWIN minimum sub-window length.
37	    """
38	
39	    def __init__(self, delta: float = 0.002, num_samples: int = 10000,
40	                 change_point: int = 5000, sigma: float = 1.0,
41	                 max_buckets_per_row: int = 5, min_window_length: int = 10):
42	        self.delta = float(delta)
43	        self.num_samples = int(num_samples)
44	        self.change_point = int(change_point)
45	        self.sigma = float(sigma)
46	        self.max_buckets_per_row = int(max_buckets_per_row)
47	        self.min_window_length = int(min_window_length)
48	
49	    # -- detector ----------------------------------------------------------
50	    def new_detector(self, delta: Optional[float] = None) -> ADWIN:
51	        return ADWIN(delta=self.delta if delta is None else delta,
52	                     max_buckets_per_row=self.max_buckets_per_row,
53	                     min_window_length=self.min_window_length)
54	
55	    # -- stream generators -------------------------------------------------
56	    def generate_stationary_stream(self, seed: int = 1,
57	                                   num_samples: Optional[int] = None,
58	                                   mean: float = 0.0,
59	                                   sigma: Optional[float] = None) -> List[float]:
60	        """A stream with no drift at all: ``N(mean, sigma)``."""
61	        rng = random.Random(seed)
62	        sigma = self.sigma if sigma is None else sigma
63	        n = self.num_samples if num_samples is None else num_samples
64	        return [rng.gauss(mean, sigma) for _ in range(n)]
65	
66	    def generate_abrupt_stream(self, seed: int = 1,
67	                               num_samples: Optional[int] = None,
68	                               change_point: Optional[int] = None,
69	                               mean_before: float = 0.0,
70	                               mean_after: float = 1.0,
71	                               sigma: Optional[float] = None) -> List[float]:
72	        """A stream whose mean jumps at ``change_point``."""
73	        rng = random.Random(seed)
74	        sigma = self.sigma if sigma is None else sigma
75	        n = self.num_samples if num_samples is None else num_samples
76	        cut = self.change_point if change_point is None else change_point
77	        return [rng.gauss(mean_before if i < cut else mean_after, sigma)
78	                for i in range(n)]
79	
80	    def generate_gradual_stream(self, seed: int = 1,
81	                                num_samples: Optional[int] = None,
82	                                change_start: Optional[int] = None,
83	                                transition_length: int = 1000,
84	                                mean_before: float = 0.0,
85	                                mean_after: float = 1.0,
86	                                sigma: Optional[float] = None) -> List[float]:
87	        """A stream whose mean ramps linearly from one level to the other."""
88	        rng = random.Random(seed)
89	        sigma = self.sigma if sigma is None else sigma
90	        n = self.num_samples if num_samples is None else num_samples
91	        start = self.change_point if change_start is None else change_start
92	        data: List[float] = []
93	        for i in range(n):
94	            if i < start:
95	                mean = mean_before
96	            elif i >= start + transition_length:
97	                mean = mean_after
98	            else:
99	                progress = (i - start) / float(transition_length)
100	                mean = mean_before + progress * (mean_after - mean_before)
101	            data.append(rng.gauss(mean, sigma))
102	        return data
103	
104	    def generate_recurring_stream(self, seed: int = 1,
105	                                  num_samples: Optional[int] = None,
106	                                  period: int = 2000,
107	                                  mean_low: float = 0.0,
108	                                  mean_high: float = 1.0,
109	                                  sigma: Optional[float] = None) -> List[float]:
110	        """A stream that alternates between two concepts every ``period``."""
111	        rng = random.Random(seed)
112	        sigma = self.sigma if sigma is None else sigma
113	        n = self.num_samples if num_samples is None else num_samples
114	        data: List[float] = []
115	        for i in range(n):
116	            high = (i // period) % 2 == 1
117	            data.append(rng.gauss(mean_high if high else mean_low, sigma))
118	        return data
119	
120	    def recurring_change_points(self, num_samples: Optional[int] = None,
121	                                period: int = 2000) -> List[int]:
122	        n = self.num_samples if num_samples is None else num_samples
123	        return list(range(period, n, period))
124	
125	    # -- single run --------------------------------------------------------
126	    def run_detection(self, data: Sequence[float],
127	                      change_points: Sequence[int] = (),
128	                      delta: Optional[float] = None,
129	                      true_means: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None
130	                      ) -> Dict[str, object]:
131	        """Feed ``data`` to ADWIN and collect detection statistics.
132	
133	        Args:
134	            data: The stream of observations.
135	            change_points: Indices at which the distribution really changes.
136	            delta: Optional confidence override.
137	            true_means: Optional per-sample true mean, used to score the
138	                running estimate.
139	
140	        Returns:
141	            A dict with the detection indices, the delay for each true change
142	            point, the number of false alarms, the window trajectory and the
143	            mean estimation error.
144	        """
145	        detector = self.new_detector(delta)
146	        detections: List[int] = []
147	        widths: List[int] = []
148	        width_after_detection: List[int] = []
149	        estimation_error = 0.0
150	        for index, value in enumerate(data):
151	            changed = detector.add_element(value)
152	            widths.append(detector.width)
153	            if changed:
154	                detections.append(index)
155	                width_after_detection.append(detector.width)
156	            if true_means is not None:
157	                estimation_error += abs(detector.get_estimation()
158	                                       - true_means[index])
159	
160	        delays: List[Optional[int]] = []
161	        matched = set()
162	        for position, change in enumerate(change_points):
163	            limit = (change_points[position + 1]
164	                     if position + 1 < len(change_points) else len(data))
165	            delay = None
166	            for detection in detections:
167	                if change <= detection < limit:
168	                    # ADWIN keeps signalling while it shrinks the window, so
169	                    # every alarm up to the next true change is attributed to
170	                    # this change; the delay is the first of them.
171	                    matched.add(detection)
172	                    if delay is None:
173	                        delay = detection - change
174	            delays.append(delay)
175	        false_alarms = [d for d in detections if d not in matched]
176	
177	        return {
178	            "detections": detections,
179	            "num_detections": len(detections),
180	            "delays": delays,
181	            "false_alarms": len(false_alarms),
182	            "false_positive_rate": len(false_alarms) / max(1, len(data)),
183	            "widths": widths,
184	            "average_width": sum(widths) / max(1, len(widths)),
185	            "final_width": detector.width,
186	            "width_after_first_detection": (width_after_detection[0]
187	                                            if width_after_detection else None),
188	            "width_after_detection": width_after_detection,
189	            "final_estimation": detector.get_estimation(),
190	            "mean_estimation_error": (estimation_error / max(1, len(data))
191	                                      if true_means is not None else None),
192	            "detector": detector,
193	        }

195	    # -- experiment 1: detection delay -------------------------------------
196	    def detection_delay(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS,
197	                        mean_before: float = 0.0,
198	                        mean_after: float = 1.0) -> float:
199	        """Average number of samples between the drift and its detection."""
200	        delays: List[int] = []
201	        for seed in seeds:
202	            data = self.generate_abrupt_stream(seed=seed,
203	                                               mean_before=mean_before,
204	                                               mean_after=mean_after)
205	            result = self.run_detection(data, change_points=(self.change_point,))
206	            delay = result["delays"][0]  # type: ignore[index]
207	            if delay is None:
208	                # never detected: charge the whole remaining stream
209	                delay = len(data) - self.change_point
210	            delays.append(delay)
211	        return sum(delays) / max(1, len(delays))

213	    # -- experiment 2: false positive rate ---------------------------------
214	    def false_positive_rate(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS) -> float:
215	        """Fraction of samples on a stationary stream that raise an alarm."""
216	        rates: List[float] = []
217	        for seed in seeds:
218	            data = self.generate_stationary_stream(seed=seed)
219	            result = self.run_detection(data)
220	            rates.append(result["num_detections"] / max(1, len(data)))  # type: ignore[operator]
221	        return sum(rates) / max(1, len(rates))
222	
223	    # -- experiment 3: window size, stationary stream ----------------------
224	    def window_size_stable(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS,
225	                           num_samples: int = 5000) -> float:
226	        """Average window length while the distribution does not change."""
227	        sizes: List[float] = []
228	        for seed in seeds:
229	            data = self.generate_stationary_stream(seed=seed,
230	                                                   num_samples=num_samples)
231	            result = self.run_detection(data)
232	            sizes.append(result["average_width"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]

234	
235	    # -- experiment 4: window size right after a drift ---------------------
236	    def window_size_drift(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS,
237	                          mean_before: float = 0.0,
238	                          mean_after: float = 1.0) -> float:
239	        """Window length immediately after the drift has been detected."""

246	            width = None

249	                    width = detector.width
250	                    break

252	        return sum(sizes) / max(1, len(sizes))
253	
254	    # -- experiment 5: mean estimation error -------------------------------
255	    def mean_estimation_error(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS,
256	                              mean_before: float = 0.0,
257	                              mean_after: float = 2.0,
258	                              measure_at: int = 7000) -> float:
259	        """Absolute error of the mean estimate ``measure_at`` samples in."""
260	        errors: List[float] = []
261	        for seed in seeds:
262	            data = self.generate_abrupt_stream(seed=seed,
263	                                               num_samples=measure_at,
264	                                               mean_before=mean_before,
265	                                               mean_after=mean_after)

267	            for value in data:

269	            errors.append(abs(detector.get_estimation() - mean_after))
270	        return sum(errors) / max(1, len(errors))
271	
272	    # -- extra drift shapes ------------------------------------------------
273	    def gradual_drift_report(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS
274	                             ) -> Dict[str, float]:
275	        delays: List[int] = []
276	        for seed in seeds:

284	    def recurring_drift_report(self, seeds: Sequence[int] = DEFAULT_SEEDS,
